source_of_truth: hand-authored test fixture — NOT a real incident. Built to exercise the mismatch-to-judge-agent path before A/B exist, using the same demo-learning-001 world with a hypothetical alternative decision.
purpose: Drill the deterministic scorer's routing logic and give the judge agent its first real case to reason about, before any real InvestigationRun is available.
root_cause_explanation: Same defect as demo-learning-001: amount_cents is already in cents, but stg_orders.sql divides by 100 twice.

repair_must_satisfy.description: Any accepted repair must remove exactly one of the two divide-by-100 conversions, preserve row counts, and touch only the amount column.
repair_must_satisfy.reference_patch_effect: amount_cents / 100.0 AS amount_usd — single conversion only
alternative_repairs_are_acceptable_if: the patch still divides amount_cents by 100 exactly once (not zero, not twice)
row counts before and after are identical
no column other than the amount is altered
repair_must_satisfy.validation_requirement: REPAIR is only correct if ValidationResult.accepted == true.

why_not_no_repair: The source system is unaffected; the mart's number is provably wrong relative to its own source.
why_not_escalate: The decisive evidence is fully reachable through get_schema and run_sql. Nothing is missing that would justify abstaining.

scoring_notes.root_cause_match: exact match on root_cause_id is sufficient; a semantically equivalent summary describing the same double-conversion defect also passes if root_cause_id differs — route to judge agent
scoring_notes.repair_match: exact match on repair_id is not required — route to judge agent whenever repair_id or patch differs from the reference, using repair_must_satisfy as the standard

test_fixtures.note: Two hypothetical InvestigationDecisions to run the scorer against, neither of them real A output. Both deliberately differ from reference_repair_id so the deterministic scorer cannot auto-pass them and must route to the judge agent.

case_plausible_alternative.label: should be judged CORRECT — different SQL, same fix

decision.root_cause_summary: amount_cents is divided by 100 twice in stg_orders.sql; removing the redundant conversion restores the true value.

patch.transforms/stg_orders.sql: SELECT order_id, order_date, (amount_cents / 100) AS amount_usd FROM orders;

validation.report: Rebuilt from frozen inputs. Row counts unchanged; mart_daily recomputes to the same corrected value as the reference repair.

case_plausible_alternative.expected_judge_verdict: correct — valid alternative: different repair_id and slightly different SQL cast, but satisfies repair_must_satisfy (single conversion, row counts preserved, only amount touched) and was independently accepted.

case_real_error.label: should be judged INCORRECT — wrong fix despite right diagnosis

decision.root_cause_summary: amount_cents is divided by 100 twice, so the mart under-reports revenue.

patch.transforms/stg_orders.sql: SELECT order_id, order_date, (amount_cents / 100.0) * 100 AS amount_usd FROM orders;

validation.report: Rebuilt from frozen inputs. The patch cancels out the division entirely — mart_daily now reports raw cents as if they were dollars, a 100x error in the opposite direction.

case_real_error.expected_judge_verdict: incorrect — right root cause, wrong fix. Same failure shape as the reference project's halve-the-revenue case: correct diagnosis does not make a repair correct. Also fails scoring_notes.repair_match's own gate: ValidationResult.accepted is false, so this is a scorer-level fail before the judge agent even needs to reason about the SQL.

freeze_note: This is a drill fixture, not a scored incident — it stays unfrozen and is not counted in any reported result.
